newsitem.title: UK: Kwik Save off on nerves over shake-up costs.
newsitem.headline: Kwik Save off on nerves over shake-up costs.

text.p: Shares in discount supermarket retailer Kwik Save fell on Monday amid worries over this week's results and the size of potential one-off costs involved in a widespread restructuring programme, dealers said.
The shares were down 12-1/2p to 306-1/2p by 1128 GMT in a generally weaker food retail sector.
"It's last minute nerves ahead of the results on Thursday," said Paul Smiddy, analyst at Credit Lyonnais Laing. "It's a realisation that any restructuring is going to be fairly painful," he added.

The Financial Times on Monday raised the possibility of Kwik Save entering the lucrative own-label market as a result of the group's five-month strategic review, which is expected to be announced with the group's annual results.
"This is all a bit of a storm in a teacup...they have been in own-label before," Smiddy said.

The cut-price supermarket group is expected to announce a disappointing set of results this year, the analyst said. Profits are forecast to drop to around 82-90 million stg from 125 million a year ago and some analysts expect the dividend payout to be cut.
But most analysts will be focusing on one-off restructuring charges which could slice another 100 million stg of group profits. Widespread store closures have been widely tipped.

Elsewhere in the food retail sector, shares were similarly lacklustre. Sainsbury's lost 8-1/2p to 355p in the wake of a 14 percent decrease in interim profits last week. Analysts were also nervous amid this weekend's launch of extra reward points to its loyalty card customers.
"It's an aggressive increase in the number of points," Smiddy said. "It's going to cost a lot and the sales growth may not come through."
Others in the sector came off on the back of Sainsbury's latest move, and as fears of rising competition in the industry hotted up.
Tesco lost 4p to 325-1/2p and Safeway fell 5p to 357p.
